name: FastBackgroundCheck

steps.note: The page asks for a name and an email address and nothing about a listing, so no search is needed first. https://www.fastbackgroundcheck.com/removal redirected here on verified_on. This page carries no search box of its own; the site's people search is on the front page, which is the second capture.

choices: An authorized agent of the subject of the request
steps.note: A required dropdown, shut on the capture, whose two answers were read from that page's own markup on verified_on along with the empty Choose One placeholder that is not an answer. It carries no agent_value_literal, and the reason is in notes: the agent answer reveals three more required boxes, and a manifest has no way to say that some steps run only in that case.
The only box on the form without a required marker beside its label.
The page says the link that opens the real opt-out form is sent to this address, so it has to be an inbox the person can open.

steps.prompt: FastBackgroundCheck puts a Cloudflare check under this form. On the page as captured it cleared itself and showed Success without anything being asked. Look at it: if it says Success, tell me and I will carry on. If it is asking you for anything, do it yourself and say when it is done.
steps.note: Handed over, never worked around. Nothing here solves it. The check cleared on its own on verified_on, which is why the prompt covers both states rather than assuming the person has something to do; a check that does not clear is the site refusing, and that ends the broker.

steps.prompt: The name and email are filled in and the check is done. One box is still unticked, and it reads: I authorize FastBackgroundCheck.com to send communications relating to my privacy request to the email address(es) provided, and it certifies that you are the subject of the request or an agent authorized to act on behalf of the subject. Check the values, then say yes and I will tick that box and send the request.

selector.label: I authorize FastBackgroundCheck.com to send communications relating to my privacy request to the email address(es) provided.

steps.note: Ticked only after the gate above, because the certification is the person's to make.

steps.prompt: FastBackgroundCheck is sending a link to that address. The page says opening it brings up the opt-out form itself, which asks for the information on the record you want removed. That form is not on any page captured here, so fill it in yourself. The page says that if you wait more than 24 hours to click the link you will need to request a new one. When you reach the confirmation page, read it and tell me what it said.
steps.note: This is where the manifest stops and the broker's flow does not. Nothing has been removed at this point; only a link has been asked for. What the second form asks for is not described here, because nobody has captured it and the first page says only that it asks for information matching the record.

verification.success_when: A search of the site's own people search for this name and city no longer returns the listing. That search is on the front page, in the second capture, and its second box takes a city, which is why current_address.city is a required field even though no step on the opt-out form fills it.

additional_captures.of: The site's front page on the same visit, where the people search boxes and a button with text on it are in the open. It is the door search_url_template records, and the opt-out page has no box of its own

id_requirements.note: The first form asks for a name and an email address. No account, payment, notarised document, or photo ID appears anywhere on it. The page has a Log In button in its header and nothing on the form refers to it. What the form behind the emailed link asks for is not known, because that page was not captured.

notes: Written from the opt-out page captured on verified_on, with the front page as a second capture. Four things the page states and a run depends on. The first form only asks for a link to be emailed, and the opt-out form itself arrives at that address. If the link is not clicked within 24 hours, the page says a new one has to be requested; it does not say the old one stops working, and the manifest does not say so either. A confirmation page and a confirmation email follow the second form. The page asks people to allow 3 days for the record to come off the site, which is where recheck_after_days comes from. The Cloudflare check under the form cleared itself during the visit and showed Success without asking anything, so the captcha gate's prompt covers a check that is already done as well as one that is not; a check that does not clear is a bot wall and ends the broker. What the captures show and what they do not: the heading, the directions, every field label, the checkbox text, the Cloudflare check, and the Submit button are on the opt-out frame, and both search boxes and the Public Records Search button are on the front-page frame; the css fallbacks, the two dropdown answers, and the form's own id were read from the page's markup on the same visit, and neither image holds a browser address bar, so home_url, source_url, and optout_url record addresses that were open rather than anything legible on them. Two things were done to the opt-out page before it was captured, and neither adds or removes anything the broker wrote: ten fixed advertising containers were hidden, one of which sat beside the form, and the page was viewed zoomed out so the whole section fits one frame. The frame also stops below the Submit button, which leaves out the site's A-to-Z directory bars; they carry letters and number ranges rather than names. One thing this manifest deliberately does not do. The dropdown offers a path for an authorized agent, and choosing it reveals three further required boxes, Agent First Name, Agent Last Name and Agent Email, which sit in the page's markup already and are hidden until that answer is picked. So the missing piece is not a capture. A manifest is a straight list of steps with no way to say that three of them run only when the profile carries an authorized_agent block, so filling the agent answer would leave three required boxes empty and the form would be refused. Until that can be said, this step answers as the subject and an operator running it for somebody else stops here rather than certifying the wrong thing. No syndication note appears in this manifest. The page states no relationship to any other site, and nothing about a shared page design is evidence of one.
